test_text_surface_carries_a_banner (lines 185-190): each non-JSON GENERATED surface's first 8 lines must contain 'generated' and name GENERATED[rel]

findings.finding: The plan does not enumerate the generated-surface parity gate tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py as a consumer. That suite requires (a) the README 'Generated — never edit these by hand' table to EQUAL the GENERATED registry set exactly, and (b) each generated .md to carry a self-announcing 'generated' banner naming its generator command in its first 8 lines. Adding config-reference.md/security.md/gen_config_reference.py without registering them there and emitting banners will fail this suite.
findings.location: Plan step 2 ('update docs/README.md and docs/architecture.md navigation to link them') and Acceptance Criteria line 5
scenarios: CI/make-test runs test_generated_surface_markers.py after the new docs land; the README generated-table != GENERATED set, or the new docs lack a generator-naming banner, so the suite reds unexpectedly
findings.suggested_fix: In Plan step 2, specify: register the generator command for both docs in the GENERATED map in tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py and in the docs/README.md '### Generated — never edit these by hand' table (not just prose navigation), and have gen_config_reference.py write a top-of-file banner naming 'python scripts/gen_config_reference.py' in each generated doc.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that REQUIRED_TOPICS is defined against the epic's operator-topic contract (a fixed external list), NOT derived from the generator's emitted headings or the template constant, so the coverage test cannot become tautological.
evidence: Plan: 'a test asserts that, across docs/config-reference.md and docs/security.md together, a heading/anchor exists for every entry in an explicit REQUIRED_TOPICS list ... failing if any is missing.'

The named topics (observability exception, subprocess limitations, behavior deltas, native refresh) come from the curated template constant embedded in the generator, so if REQUIRED_TOPICS mirrors the template constant the assertion is self-satisfying.
findings.finding: The topic-coverage test asserts an anchor exists in the generated docs for every entry in a REQUIRED_TOPICS list, but the plan does not state that REQUIRED_TOPICS is pinned to the epic's operator-topic contract independently of what the generator/template emit. If the same author derives REQUIRED_TOPICS from the generator's own headings, the test degenerates into a tautology (generator emits heading X; test checks heading X exists) that passes regardless of whether the doc actually covers the intended operator topic.
findings.location: Testing (RED -> GREEN): 'a test asserts that ... a heading/anchor exists for every entry in an explicit REQUIRED_TOPICS list'
scenarios: A future edit silently drops the 'observability exception' narrative from the template AND from REQUIRED_TOPICS in the same commit; the coverage test still passes, so the operator doc loses a required topic undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare REQUIRED_TOPICS as a hardcoded literal enumerating the epic-mandated topics in the test module (not imported from the generator), and note that removing a topic from the template without updating this independent list must trip the coverage test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fold the drift check into `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` as a `--check` flag (matching gen_env_registry.py/gen_cli_reference.py) instead of adding a separate `scripts/check_config_reference_drift.py`, or justify why a standalone script is warranted here when the cited models use an in-generator flag.
evidence: Plan step 3: 'Add scripts/check_config_reference_drift.py and wire it into make lint ... modelled on the existing gen_env_registry.py --check doc-drift gate already run under make lint'
gen_env_registry.py:210-226 — main() with argparse `--check` regenerates in-memory and compares to the committed file, returning non-zero on stale; no separate check script
gen_cli_reference.py:22,244 — same in-generator `--check` flag convention
The plan simultaneously names `--check` as its model AND proposes a distinct standalone script, an internal contradiction
findings.finding: The plan adds a separate `scripts/check_config_reference_drift.py` module, but the two generators it explicitly cites as models (gen_env_registry.py, gen_cli_reference.py) both implement drift detection via an in-generator `--check` flag on the SAME module (gen_env_registry.py main() lines 210-224; gen_cli_reference.py --check at line 244), not a second script. This reinvents an established, understood drift-check convention and is internally inconsistent with the plan's own claim to be 'modelled on the existing gen_env_registry.py --check doc-drift gate'.
findings.location: Plan step 3 / AC line 'The drift check runs under make lint'

findings.suggested_fix: Implement drift detection as a `--check` argument on `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` (regenerate in-memory, newline-normalized compare to the committed files, non-zero exit on stale), exactly as gen_env_registry.py's main() does, and wire `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py --check` into make lint. Drop the separate check script from the plan and rollback list.
